It hands out the same kind of access token Supabase Auth would, and the API checks it exactly as it would check a real one: what each person may see and do below is what a real sign-in would get.

data.name: whoami.intro
data.value: GET /me, as {0} in {1}: the seat the API resolved from your token and the Tenant header, where it is placed, the roles it holds there for which period, and every key it holds now with the units each one reaches.

data.name: whoami.no-answer
data.value: The API did not say who you are in this tenant. This is its answer:

data.name: whoami.placements
data.value: Placements and the roles held there

data.name: whoami.roles.none
data.value: No organization roles. Crew roles on projects are shown with each project.

data.name: whoami.grants-manage
data.value: Where you hold {0} you give any role that manages no access to anyone placed there or below, yourself included, without holding its keys: to others for as long as you choose, to yourself for no longer than you hold {0}. A role that manages access needs each of its keys that manage access, held by you there for at least as long, and is never yours to give yourself.

data.name: whoami.seats-manage
data.value: Holding {0} for the whole tenant you suspend, reactivate and deactivate seats, and may suspend or deactivate your own. A seat whose grants include a role that manages access needs, for each of those grants, the role's keys that manage access, held by you at that grant's unit until at least its end: stopping or restarting the seat takes the role away or gives it back.

data.name: whoami.units-manage
data.value: Where you hold {0} at a unit's parent and at another unit, you move the unit there. A move gives you no key you do not hold at the unit already, for as long, and gives or takes away a key that manages access, from anyone, only when you hold it at the unit for at least as long as their grant runs.

data.name: whoami.keys-now.none
data.value: None. A grant that has expired, a suspended seat or an archived role gives no key.

data.name: projects.intro
data.value: GET /projects: every project you may see in {0}, and how. Crew means you are on its crew, with a role or without, and is what the list says when a role of yours reaches the project as well; organization means through a role you hold at its unit or above. A project you may not see is not listed, in this tenant or any other. The answer names units, seats and project roles by their ids; the names shown here come from the directory, POST /tenancy/directory/…, asked with those ids, and from GET /project-roles. The list comes a page at a time, by number: More asks the next page with the marker the last one gave.

data.name: projects.filter.text
data.value: Number starts with, or name contains

data.name: projects.none
data.value: There is no project you may see here.

data.name: project.not-shown
data.value: The API did not show this project. A project in another tenant, or one you may not see, is not found, exactly as one that does not exist.

data.name: project.seen-no-role
data.value: , on its crew with no role

data.name: project.not-planned
data.value: Not planned for any days yet.

data.name: project.can
data.value: What the API says you may do:

data.name: project.crew.intro
data.value: Being on the crew and holding a role on it are two things, each with its own dates. A seat on the crew sees the project. What else it may do comes from the roles it holds there, each for a period of its own, and only while it is on the crew.

data.name: project.crew.roles-not-shown
data.value: Which roles each member holds, and until when, is shown to whoever manages the crew.

data.name: project.crew.no-role
data.value: on the crew, with no role

data.name: project.plan.help
data.value: The days the work is planned for, first and last; both blank takes the plan away. An inspection then covers days within them.

data.name: project.add.label
data.value: Put a seat on the crew

data.name: project.add.no-role
data.value: (no role: sees the project, nothing more)

data.name: project.add.help
data.value: Any active seat of the tenant, your own included, until the day picked or for good. A role picked here is given for the same period.

data.name: project.give.help
data.value: Next to the roles the member holds, until the day picked or for good; take one away in the crew table. You need not hold the role's keys yourself, and may give one to yourself. On a crew a role gives only what acts on this project; opening projects and naming the owner come from the organization. The list holds the tenant's project roles in use: a role of the organization is refused on a crew, which the try-it page shows.

data.name: project.reopen.help
data.value: Whoever may close a project may reopen it.

data.name: project.inspect.help
data.value: The days it covers, first and last; both blank is the day it is recorded, by the clock in UTC, which east or west of it may be another day than today. On a planned project they lie within its planned days, or the API refuses.

data.name: try.intro
data.value: Send any call the API has, as yourself, as nobody, or in any tenant, and see what it decides: the status and, for a refusal, its code. The presets below do on purpose what their person may not.

data.name: try.action.check-key
data.value: Check a key on a project

data.name: try.action.units-with-key
data.value: Units where I hold a key

data.name: try.no-token
data.value: No token: call anonymously (never signs you out)

data.name: try.presets.intro
data.value: Each runs as its person, with that person's token from the dev login, and leaves your own sign-in alone. Every one is a refusal of the demonstration as it is seeded, or a read that is allowed beside the same read refused, so running them changes nothing. A role you give from this UI first can make one succeed.

data.name: try.history.none
data.value: Nothing sent yet in this session.

data.name: history.intro
data.value: GET /tenancy/history: every change to who may do what in {0}, newest first, each with who made it. Reading it takes the key tenancy.history.view for the whole tenant; without it the API refuses, and the refusal is shown here. A row names seats, units and roles by their ids, and never says why a role was given; the name shown for who acted comes from the directory. The list comes a page at a time: More asks the next page with the marker the last one gave.

data.name: history.none
data.value: Nothing has changed anyone's access yet.

data.name: invitations.intro
data.value: GET /tenancy/invitations: the invitations into {0} that can still be accepted, for whoever manages seats at their unit. Inviting takes the keys tenancy.seats.manage for the whole tenant and tenancy.grants.manage at the unit, and the role is held to the rule every grant is held to; without them the API refuses, and the refusal is shown here. No seat is made until the person accepts.

data.name: invitations.invite.label
data.value: A seat in a unit, with a role there, for the person at an address

data.name: invitations.invite.name
data.value: Name for the seat; left empty, the person gives one when accepting

data.name: invitations.invite.help
data.value: The invitation stays open for a week. A role with an end must end after that week. The answer says nothing of whether the address has an account already.

data.name: invitations.issued.title
data.value: Invited. What follows is shown this once.

data.name: invitations.issued.text
data.value: Hand this link to the person, unless a mail from Supabase Auth brings it: a new account gets it by mail where the Host knows this UI's address. It carries the invitation's token, of which the API keeps only a digest, so nobody can show it again. It works until {0}, for the account with the invited address, once signed in.

data.name: invitations.issued.token
data.value: Or the token alone, to paste on the page "Accept an invitation":

data.name: accept.intro
data.value: POST /invitations/accept: {0} accepts the invitation a token is for, and has a seat, its placement and its role from that one call on. The call names no tenant: the token says which. The API refuses a token that was revoked, that somebody else used or whose week ran out, and one sent to another address than this account's.

data.name: accept.name
data.value: Name for the seat: needed when the invitation suggests none

data.name: accept.help
data.value: A link to this page carries the token after the #. Open it signed in, or paste the token here.

data.name: accept.done
data.value: Accepted: a seat in {0}, where this session now works.

data.name: accept.sign-in-first
data.value: Accepting takes a sign-in with the invited address: sign in, then open the link again or paste its token here. The link in a mail from Supabase Auth signs its person in by itself.

data.name: accept.link.refused
data.value: Supabase Auth did not take the link in the mail: it works once, and for a limited time. Whoever chose a password with it signs in on the login page; otherwise a new invitation is needed.

data.name: accept.link.asks
data.value: This link signs in {0}, and this tab is signed in as {1}. Nothing has changed. Take the link only when it came from a mail that was sent to you: anybody can make a link that signs in an account of their own.

data.name: accept.password.intro
data.value: The link in the mail signed {0} in, this once. With a password the next sign-in is on the login page. It goes to Supabase Auth (PUT user) and is kept nowhere here. The invitation is next.

data.name: accept.password.done
data.value: The password is set: the next sign-in is on the login page, with the address and that password.

data.name: login.link.refused
data.value: Supabase Auth does not know the sign-in this link carries.

data.name: login.password.not-taken
data.value: Supabase Auth did not take that password: it asks for a longer or a less common one.

data.name: login.password.session-over
data.value: The sign-in the link gave has ended, so no password was set.

data.name: project-roles.intro
data.value: GET /project-roles: the roles {0} keeps for its crews, archived ones too. A crew member holds one on one project, and it gives only what acts on that project. The starter roles were made when the tenant was set up; the tenant renames, re-keys and archives them, and makes its own. Anybody who works in the tenant reads their names. Their keys, and making and changing a role, are for whoever holds tenancy.roles.manage for the whole tenant; the API refuses anybody else, and the refusal is shown here.

data.name: project-roles.none
data.value: The tenant has no crew roles.

data.name: project-roles.make.label
data.value: A name, what it is for, and the keys it gives on a crew

data.name: project-roles.make.help
data.value: Only keys that act on a project go on a crew role: a key of the organization is refused, which shows here.

data.name: project-roles.change.help
data.value: Renaming sets the name and what it is for together: a description left empty is cleared. The keys become exactly the ones picked, none taking them all off. An archived role changes no more, and the crew lead's role is not archived: every project's owner holds it.
